about: What the `lua` selection of SCE_SCRIPT_ENGINE answers differently from
ECMA-262, case by case, against the shared table beside this file.
The engine that selection reaches is Lua 5.4 with
`EcmaScriptToLuaTransformer` rewriting the author's ECMAScript into Lua
text. It is a listed, validated value of the cache entry, so a consumer
may build with it; the default is `quickjs`, which answers every case in
the shared table.
This file exists because the count used to live in prose. A comment said
26 of 58 on the day someone measured it, the shared table then grew to 98
cases, and nothing re-answered the question: the real number on
2026-08-18 was 44. A list the test reads cannot drift that way. An entry
here that starts agreeing fails as loudly as a case that starts
disagreeing, so neither direction passes unnoticed.
`needs` says what closing an entry would take, and it is nearly the same
answer every time:
operand-boundaries  A rewriting pass replaces text without knowing
where an operand ends. `a && b` cannot yield its
left operand, `1 == '1'` cannot coerce, and
`-7 % 3` cannot truncate, because no pass can say
what `a`, `1` or `-7` extend to. Closing these
means parsing the expression, which SCE already
does once, in the build-time frontend that every
generated backend shares.
chain-operand       The operand of a prefix operator is the whole
member and call chain after it, not the first name
in it.
statement-structure A statement form the script pipeline does not read.
The divergences that were not of that kind have been repaired rather than
listed: member calls the shared runtime library already defined, a string
literal no pass could see as a receiver, a computed index that was never
shifted, `Math.round`, and `\uXXXX`. Those took 44 disagreements to 23.
